hyperedges.label: SSL Renewal Coordination: UFW + Certbot + Nginx
Layered Security Model (UFW static + fail2ban dynamic + CouchDB auth)

nodes.label: Flexible Network Architecture Pattern
nodes.rationale: Three network modes (shared/isolated/custom) allow integration with existing Docker services or standalone deployment, avoiding single-mode constraint. Subnet auto-allocation (172.24-31.0.0/16) prevents conflicts.

nodes.label: Certbot UFW Hook Pattern
nodes.rationale: Port 80 is kept closed by default and opened only transiently via certbot pre/post renewal hooks. This minimizes attack surface while enabling Let's Encrypt HTTP-01 validation.

nodes.label: Localhost-Only Backend Port Binding
nodes.rationale: CouchDB (5984) and ServerPeer (3000) bind to 127.0.0.1 only. All external access is routed through nginx reverse proxy. This eliminates direct external exposure of backend services.

nodes.label: Nostr Room ID Vault Isolation Pattern
nodes.rationale: A single shared Nostr Relay routes signaling messages by Room ID subscription, giving vault isolation without deploying separate relay instances per vault. Actual file data never passes through the relay.
nodes.norm_label: nostr room id vault isolation pattern

nodes.label: Nginx WebSocket Support for CouchDB Changes Feed
nodes.rationale: Official CouchDB nginx documentation lacks WebSocket upgrade support, breaking real-time _changes feed sync. The project adds Upgrade/Connection headers and HTTP/1.1 to fix this, exceeding official recommendations.
nodes.norm_label: nginx websocket support for couchdb changes feed

nodes.label: Docker Image ID Comparison for Update Detection
nodes.rationale: Image ID (Config.Digest) is used rather than manifest digest to detect needed updates, because manifest digests differ for multi-arch images while Image ID matches Docker's own pull-needed determination logic.
nodes.norm_label: docker image id comparison for update detection

nodes.label: Pre-pull Workaround for BuildKit Proxy Limitation
nodes.rationale: Docker daemon proxy settings do not propagate to BuildKit's separate buildkitd daemon. Pre-pulling base images via docker pull (which respects daemon proxy) before docker build ensures images are available from cache without requiring BuildKit proxy configuration.
nodes.norm_label: pre-pull workaround for buildkit proxy limitation

nodes.label: CouchDB Single-Node Mode
nodes.rationale: single_node=true simplifies deployment and eliminates cluster coordination overhead for a self-hosted single-server use case

nodes.label: CouchDB require_valid_user Security Enforcement
nodes.rationale: require_valid_user=true ensures all HTTP endpoints require authentication, preventing unauthenticated access to the database

nodes.label: fail2ban UFW Dynamic Rule Injection
nodes.rationale: Using UFW as banaction lets fail2ban insert deny rules at position 1 (highest priority) without replacing static UFW rules, maintaining compatibility with certbot hooks

nodes.label: fail2ban Backend-Aware Jail Configuration
nodes.rationale: Jails are conditionally created based on SYNC_BACKEND to avoid monitoring unavailable services and prevent false alarms

nodes.label: Image ID vs Manifest Digest Comparison Strategy
nodes.rationale: Using Config.Digest (Image ID) instead of manifest digest for update detection because manifest LIST digest differs from platform-specific digest for multi-arch images, causing false positives
nodes.norm_label: image id vs manifest digest comparison strategy

nodes.label: Shared Network Mode Variant
nodes.rationale: Shared mode enables integration with existing nginx/services on the same Docker network without requiring a dedicated subnet

nodes.label: Isolated Network Mode Variant
nodes.rationale: Isolated mode creates a dedicated obsidian_network for maximum security, preventing lateral movement from other containers

nodes.label: env-file chmod 600 Security Design
nodes.rationale: Restricting .env to owner read/write prevents credential leakage from other system users or compromised processes

nodes.label: Backend-Aware S3 Backup Prefix Configuration
nodes.rationale: Dual mode uses separate S3 prefixes (COUCHDB_S3_BACKUP_PREFIX and SERVERPEER_S3_BACKUP_PREFIX) to prevent file conflicts when both backends upload to the same S3 bucket

nodes.label: Conditional .env Variable Generation per Backend
nodes.rationale: Backend-specific variables are only written to .env when their backend is selected to avoid unbound variable errors in scripts that source .env

nodes.label: PEP 668 Compliant Python Dependency Installation
nodes.rationale: Using apt-get install python3-boto3 instead of pip3 respects PEP 668 (externally-managed-environment) on Ubuntu 23.04+ which blocks pip from modifying system Python packages

nodes.label: Deny-by-Default Firewall Policy
nodes.rationale: Deny-by-default minimizes attack surface; only ports 22 (SSH) and 443 (HTTPS) are permanently open, with port 80 opened only transiently during certbot renewal

nodes.label: Dual Backend Support Concept (CouchDB + ServerPeer)
nodes.rationale: Supporting both CouchDB (client-server) and ServerPeer (P2P/WebRTC) backends enables users to choose their sync topology based on requirements: reliability vs. P2P privacy

nodes.label: Graceful Degradation (P2P works offline)
nodes.rationale: P2P sync via WebRTC continues functioning even when ServerPeer is offline because clients connect directly; ServerPeer is only an always-on buffer
